items.title: Devise better system but no reversion to government: Ex-Justice Rohinton Nariman on Collegium
items.summary: Former Supreme Court Justice Rohinton Nariman recently said that the criticism levelled at the Collegium system of appointing judges to the High Courts and the Supreme Court is not misplaced, and he is all for a better system of appointing judges. However, returning the power of judicial appointment to the government would severely compromise the independence of the judiciary, he warned. “Now there are lots of pot shots being thrown at the Collegium system today rightly. If anybody can devise a better system of appointment, I am all for it (but) certainly not reversion to government, no way,” Justice Nariman said. He also criticised the 103rd Constitutional Amendment, arguing that extending economic reservations to upper castes turns constitutional principles on their head. He warned that India’s constitutional institutions are currently experiencing a great decline. “The institutions today that the Constitution has laid down are unfortunately in great decline," Justice Nariman said. Collegium system Justice Nariman acknowledged valid criticisms surrounding judicial appointments. However, he firmly cautioned against restoring executive control over the appointment process. items.title: Disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens intrinsically arbitrary; no amount of whataboutery can justify it: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan
items.summary: Supreme Court Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said that any process which disenfranchises millions of Indian citizens is intrinsically arbitrary and a negation of the constitutional order. No whataboutery can justify the act of taking away voting rights of citizens, he criticised. "If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary. No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution and I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution of India," he said. Justice Bhuyan was delivering the valedictory address at the 19th NALSAR-Justice BR Sawhney Memorial Moot Court Competition at NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad. items.title: Right to vote in great peril: Justice Rohinton Nariman flags executive interference in Election Commission
items.summary: Former Supreme Court Justice Rohinton Nariman has expressed grave concern over the functioning of the Election Commission of India (ECI), particularly large scale voter exclusion and executive interference in appointments to the electoral body. In a speech delivered on September 27, Justice warned that the citizens's right to vote is facing unprecedented threats. “The common man today under our Constitution, and if I may say so, the heart of our Constitution, the heart of our democracy, which is the right to vote, is in great peril,” Justice Nariman stated. He pointed out that an astounding number of 90 lakh were disenfranchised. 22 lakh affected citizens filed appeals against the ECI decision, and among the 1 lakh appeals decided, an overwhelming 93 percent verdicts eventually came in favour of the excluded, he said. “So can you imagine, this was a completely illegal knocking out of the common man, of the citizen of India, in order that a government obtains what it wants. And the result of that you saw in West Bengal was something that upset the government of the day and brought in the government of the centre,” he said. items.title: A Fundamental Right
items.summary: With its new law that makes education a fundamental right with effect from April 1, 2010, India joins a small group of countries with such a statutory provision. All children in the 6 to 14 age group can exercise the right under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009. An estimated one crore children who do not go to school now are expected to benefit.

items.title: RSS mouthpiece asks if protest against ECI is CIA ploy to destabilise BJP regime
items.summary: Organiser, the mouthpiece of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), has claimed that a CIA plot may be behind the protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the conduct of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls by the Election Commission of India (ECI). It compared the protests to the 2024 Gen Z revolution in Bangladesh that led to the ouster of then Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. In an article titled ‘ECI controversy resembles Bangladesh regime change playbook; Is it a CIA conspiracy to destabilise India?’, the magazine posed the question without citing any source or document. It asked whether the ongoing protests against SIR were the “first step in the larger plot weaved by the hidden hands”. Organiser claimed that the allegations of irregularities and a fractured consensus in the ECI revisit a pattern seen in Bangladesh. It claimed that “intelligence sources” and “geopolitical analysts” believe that the CIA targeted Bangladesh’s Election Commission first.
